rationale: The workflow is a weekly scheduled dependency security audit (rustsec/audit-check) with a single job and no dependency installation, build, or test steps. Candidate optimizations were checked against the provided evidence and repository files: P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE (suppress schedules during inactivity) is contraindicated because security/time-based requirements need fresh checks and new advisories can be published without repository changes; P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER (filter triggers by changed paths) is contraindicated because dependencies and advisories affect unrelated paths, so skipping on no source change would miss new vulnerabilities; P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads) is not applicable because there is no measurable repeated dependency fetch/install step to cache, only checkout and audit. The pip-cache experiment (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2, P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE) concerns a Python test workflow and does not transfer to this Rust audit workflow. No supported optimization preserves the intended security-audit coverage, so the workflow is left unchanged.
